claims.claim_ar: توكيد إعجاز القرآن بتحدٍّ بلاغيّ: «أْتُوا بِسورةٍ مثلِه» كحجة على عدم إمكان الافتراء
claims.claim_en: Asserting the Qur'an's inimitability by a rhetorical challenge: 'Bring a surah like it' — used as an argument against claims of fabrication.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Strengthens the claim of divine origin by issuing a direct rhetorical challenge that highlights human inability to match the text's eloquence.

claims.claim_type: توكيد على العربية والاستقامة (emphasis on Arabic eloquence)
claims.claim_ar: تأكيد على كون النص (القرآن) عربيّاً سليمَ الصياغة، لا اعوجاج فيه — أي بلاغة واستقامة في اللفظ والمعنى
claims.claim_en: Emphasis on the text's Arabicness and straightness (no 'crookedness') — asserting linguistic purity and stylistic perfection.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Highlights authenticity and aesthetic perfection of the wording, reinforcing the listener's recognition of its superior style.

claims.claim_ar: استعمال صيغة شرطية تعظيمية (لو/لئن) لعمل تنديد وإنذار؛ صياغة افتراضية قوية تبيّن مدى تأثير وقوع الأمر لو حدث
claims.claim_en: Use of an emphatic hypothetical conditional (e.g., 'لو/لئن') as a rhetorical device for admonition/warning; a hypothetical construction used to intensify the point by imagining an extreme consequence.
claims.needs_review_reason: Mapping of 'وَلَئِنِ' (لأنّ/لئن) in this ayah to the examples using 'لو' in the commentary is interpretive; review recommended to confirm whether the commentary's 'لو' example is being read as the same rhetorical function as 'لئن'.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates a vivid hypothetical to warn the addressee about following desires after receiving knowledge, thereby increasing the moral pressure of the statement.
